name: HunterDomainSearch
title: Hunter Domain Search
description: List every known email address at one domain or company
whenToUse: Pick to list EVERY known email address at one domain or company, for exhaustive coverage of a single known domain. Use it when you have a domain and want all its addresses; finding one person's address, verifying deliverability, full profiles, or role-filtered people across companies are different jobs.

package.name: gtm
package.packageFile:
$schema: ../_schema/package.schema.json

# Two vendors, one package: Apollo.io for company and people data, Hunter.io for email.
# One credential each, one base URL each, no SDKs.
#
# The retired TypeScript is at `_legacy/nodes/gtm/`.

name: gtm
displayName: Go To Market
description: Company and people discovery, enrichment and email verification
version: 2.0.0
category: productivity
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1775374180/gravity/icons/apollo.jpg

features:
  - Apollo company and people search, with filters
  - Apollo company and people enrichment
  - Hunter email discovery, finding and verification

allowedHosts:
  - api.apollo.io
  - api.hunter.io

requires:
  credential: [apiKeyHeader, apiKeyQuery]
  transport: [json]
  paginate: [page]
  executorVersion: ">=1.4.0"

credentials.apolloCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

name: apolloCredential
displayName: Apollo.io
description: Apollo.io master API key for people and organisation search
documentationUrl: https://docs.apollo.io/docs/create-api-key

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Apollo.io master API key, required for the search endpoints
    placeholder: ""
credentials.hunterCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

name: hunterCredential
displayName: Hunter.io
description: Hunter.io API key for email discovery, verification and enrichment
documentationUrl: https://hunter.io/api-documentation/v2

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Hunter.io API key, found under API in your Hunter dashboard
    placeholder: ""

shared.apollo.yaml:
# What every Apollo call shares.
#
# The key travels in the `x-api-key` HEADER, which is `apiKeyHeader`, an executor
# capability. `Cache-Control: no-cache` is sent because the retired client sent it: Apollo
# is documented as caching search responses, and dropping the header would silently change
# which results come back.

credential: &credential
  scheme: apiKeyHeader
  header: x-api-key
  value: "{{ credentials.apolloCredential.apiKey }}"

headers: &headers
  Cache-Control: no-cache

# NOTE for the bodies below: every filter is a comma-separated config field turned into the
# array Apollo wants, with
#
#   String(config.x || '').split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean)
#
# and an EMPTY array is left out of the body rather than sent, because Apollo reads an empty
# filter as "match nothing" rather than as "no filter". That is why each body is built by an
# expression that assembles only the keys that have values, instead of a static object.
shared.hunter.yaml:
# What every Hunter call shares.
#
# TWO auth styles, and that is Hunter's doing rather than ours: `/discover` takes the key in
# an X-API-KEY header, every other endpoint takes it as an `api_key` query parameter. Both
# are executor capabilities, so each call names the one its endpoint wants.

queryCredential: &queryCredential
  scheme: apiKeyQuery
  param: api_key
  value: "{{ credentials.hunterCredential.apiKey }}"

headerCredential: &headerCredential
  scheme: apiKeyHeader
  header: X-API-KEY
  value: "{{ credentials.hunterCredential.apiKey }}"

# Hunter wraps every payload in `data` and reports failures in `errors`, sometimes with a
# 200. Without this a quota error would emit an empty result and read as "not found".
error: &error
  when: "return !!(response.errors && response.errors.length)"
  message: "return response.errors.map(e => e.details || e.id).join('; ')"

# A LinkedIn URL to the handle Hunter wants. split/join rather than a regex, because the
# expression sandbox takes no regex literal: everything after /in/, up to a ? or #, with any
# trailing slash removed.
linkedinHandle: &linkedinHandle >-
  return String(config.linkedinHandle || '').trim()
    .split('/in/').slice(-1)[0]
    .split('?')[0].split('#')[0]
    .split('/').filter(Boolean).slice(-1)[0] || ''

files.api/events.yaml:
- emit: emails
  from: response
  value: >-
    return ((response.data || {}).emails || []).map(e => ({
      value: e.value || "",
      type: e.type,
      confidence: e.confidence,
      first_name: e.first_name,
      last_name: e.last_name,
      position: e.position,
      seniority: e.seniority,
      department: e.department,
      linkedin: e.linkedin,
      twitter: e.twitter,
      phone_number: e.phone_number,
      verification: e.verification
    }))

# The domain's own metadata, minus the email list, which is already its own connector.
- emit: organization
  from: response
  value: >-
    return {
      domain: (response.data || {}).domain || "",
      organization: (response.data || {}).organization || "",
      industry: (response.data || {}).industry || null,
      country: (response.data || {}).country || null,
      state: (response.data || {}).state || null,
      city: (response.data || {}).city || null,
      linkedin: (response.data || {}).linkedin || null,
      twitter: (response.data || {}).twitter || null,
      facebook: (response.data || {}).facebook || null,
      disposable: !!(response.data || {}).disposable,
      webmail: !!(response.data || {}).webmail
    }

- emit: pattern
  from: response
  value: "return (response.data || {}).pattern || ''"

- emit: totalResults
  from: response
  value: "return ((response.meta || {}).results) || 0"

- emit: limit
  from: response
  value: "return Math.round(config.limit || 10)"

- emit: offset
  from: response
  value: "return Math.round(config.offset || 0)"
files.api/run.yaml:
# One page, with the caller choosing limit and offset. Not a walk: a large domain can hold
# thousands of addresses and each one costs credits, so paging is the operator's decision
# rather than something the node does on its own. The retired code made the same choice.

- name: search
  method: GET
  url: https://api.hunter.io/v2/domain-search
  credential: { $ref: hunter#queryCredential }
  query:
    domain: "return String(config.domain || '').trim()"
    company: "return String(config.company || '').trim()"
    type: "return String(config.type || '').trim()"
    department: "return String(config.department || '').trim()"
    seniority: "return String(config.seniority || '').trim()"
    required_field: "return String(config.requiredField || '').trim()"
    limit: "return String(Math.round(config.limit || 10))"
    offset: "return String(Math.round(config.offset || 0))"
  transport: json
  error: { $ref: hunter#error }
  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]
files.config.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: []
  properties:
    domain:
      type: string
      title: Domain
      description: The company domain, e.g. 'google.com'
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    company:
      type: string
      title: Company
      description: The company name, when you do not have the domain
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    type:
      type: string
      title: Email Type
      description: Restrict to personal or generic addresses
      enum: ["", personal, generic]
      enumNames: [Any, Personal, Generic]
      default: ""
    department:
      type: string
      title: Department
      description: Restrict to a department, e.g. 'executive, it, sales'
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    seniority:
      type: string
      title: Seniority
      description: Restrict to a seniority, e.g. 'junior, senior, executive'
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    requiredField:
      type: string
      title: Required Field
      description: Only return addresses that carry this field
      enum: ["", full_name, position, phone_number]
      enumNames: [None, Full name, Position, Phone number]
      default: ""
    limit:
      type: number
      title: Limit
      description: Addresses per page
      default: 10
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 100
    offset:
      type: number
      title: Offset
      description: Where to start, for paging through a large domain
      default: 0
      minimum: 0

    # WHO MAY RUN THIS BOX, set by whoever builds the workflow (15-who-can-run-it.md).
    #
    # INSTANCE config, not the manifest's `auth`, and the two answer different questions.
    # The manifest is the node author's FLOOR: "this node is inherently privileged". These
    # are the builder's, per box on the canvas, because the same node type legitimately
    # faces staff on one workflow and customers on another.
    #
    # A role especially has to live here: `finance:approve` is a claim THIS deployment's
    # identity provider mints, and a node published to the marketplace cannot know the role
    # vocabulary of every universe that installs it.
    #
    # The executor takes the STRICTER of the two. Neither can loosen the other.
    authRequired:
      type: boolean
      title: Require sign-in
      description: Only signed-in callers can run this step.
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
    authRole:
      type: string
      title: Require role
      description: A claim the caller must carry, like finance:approve.
      default: ""
      "ui:dependencies": { authRequired: true }

"ui:order":
  [authRequired, authRole, domain, company, type, department, seniority, requiredField, limit, offset]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: Trigger. The domain usually templates from upstream output.

outputs:
  - name: emails
    type: array
    description: Found addresses with owner name, position, seniority and confidence
  - name: organization
    type: object
    description: Company metadata for the domain (name, industry, location, socials)
  - name: pattern
    type: string
    description: The detected address pattern, e.g. '{first}.{last}'
  - name: totalResults
    type: number
    description: How many addresses Hunter holds for this domain, which may exceed the page
  - name: limit
    type: number
    description: Page size used
  - name: offset
    type: number
    description: Offset used

credentials:
  - name: hunterCredential
    required: true
    displayName: Hunter.io
files.node.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/node.schema.json

type: HunterDomainSearch
kind: PromiseNode
name: Hunter Domain Search
category: Go To Market
color: "#FF5500"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1781366295/gravity/icons/hunter.png
description: List every known email address at one domain or company
whenToUse: >
  Pick to list EVERY known email address at one domain or company, for exhaustive coverage
  of a single known domain. Use it when you have a domain and want all its addresses;
  finding one person's address, verifying deliverability, full profiles, or role-filtered
  people across companies are different jobs.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  cacheable: true

# One vendor. The package allows Apollo too, for its other four nodes.
allowedHosts: [api.hunter.io]
files.test.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/test.schema.json

testData:
  config:
    domain: close.io
    company: ""
    type: ""
    department: ""
    seniority: ""
    requiredField: ""
    limit: 5
    offset: 0
  inputs:
    signal: {}
  expect:
    emails: "return Array.isArray(output.emails)"
    organization: "return output.organization.domain === 'close.io'"
    limit: "return output.limit === 5"
